metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.limitations: Several corroborating sources are SEO/marketing blog posts (Netguru, Medium, s3corp, ksolves, avidclan, techdatapark) rather than primary engineering sources; these were used only to corroborate breadth of named adopters already anchored by the official go.dev case-studies hub and independently verifiable CNCF/Wikipedia project pages, per the predeclared two-route rule. The '75% of CNCF projects' and 'million users' figures are self-reported by the Go team and are cited as declared, limited-weight context rather than the primary basis for the score.
metric.production_adoption_deployment_ev.selection_rule: Use public, independently checkable production evidence; named deployments must be documented by the deploying organization or corroborated by credible independent sources. Popularity surveys alone do not prove deployment.

metric.third_party_tool_availability.candidate_universe: Preserved candidate universe and findings from certified legacy work unit ecosystem-external--part-2--go; recertification did not select a new language-specific target.

component_findings.build_test_coverage: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--go): Go scores 94/100: near-complete coverage across all major third-party tool categories (IDE/editor plugins from at least two independent vendors, a dedicated commercial IDE, an official debugger, multiple mature and actively maintained linters/meta-linters, and official static analysis/formatting/vulnerability tools), all either officially endorsed by the Go team via go.dev/wiki or used as the de facto industry standard in major Go projects. Points withheld only because some listed tools (e.g., golint, gometalinter) are explicitly deprecated, showing some tool churn.
component_findings.ci_devops: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-2--go): Additional widely used static analysis/format tools identified: go vet (official static analyzer), staticcheck, gofmt/goimports/gofumpt, govulncheck (vulnerability scanner using OSV.dev data), each cataloged on the official Go Wiki CodeTools page and third-party tool-aggregator analysis-tools.dev, which lists 111 cataloged Go static analysis tools, linters, and formatters.

metric.third_party_tool_availability.limitations: Findings rely on secondary blog/aggregator commentary in addition to official Go Wiki and JetBrains pages; tool-count and 'most popular' claims (e.g., 50+ linters bundled, 111 cataloged tools) are self-reported by tool vendors/aggregators and are cited only as declared context, not as a standalone popularity proxy.
metric.third_party_tool_availability.selection_rule: Inspect the same fixed tool categories for every language and require independently maintained current tools; official first-party tools may be cited only as context, not as third-party availability.
